sections_target.text: This document sets out the steps for fitting mid-span joints for AAAC alloy conductors on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.

The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

rows: A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards.
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc.
No more than one mid-span joint shall be made in one phase of one span.
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc.
Mid-span joints shall be at a distance greater than 30 m from the suspension or tension clamp (for high and extra high voltage).

Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression.
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc.
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them.
Make sure the die represents the correct size.
Make sure the inner cavity of the joint is completely clean.
Make sure the conductor ends are sound; if there is damage, cut off the damaged part.

Clean all parts of the conductor strands to be compressed, especially for greased conductors or old conductors; in the first case use a suitable solvent, and in the other case use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.
Put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of the joint, then put the conductors into the joint so that they reach the mark made previously (Figure x1a).

Compress the joint starting from the middle (Figure x1b) after leaving a distance of 2 cm from the centre on both sides, then continue compressing alternately from both sides until they overlap, and make sure of the appropriate pressure value shown on the pressure gauge.
Make sure the joint being compressed is completely horizontal so that it does not bend.
Clean the surface of the joint with a file so that there are no protrusions on the surface of the joint.

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for fitting mid-span joints for AAAC alloy conductors on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.
The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions
A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards. | 
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc. | 
The following shall be observed:
No more than one mid-span joint shall be made in one phase of one span. | 
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc. | 
Mid-span joints shall be at a distance greater than 30 m from the suspension or tension clamp (for high and extra high voltage). | 
Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression. | 
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc. | 
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation. | 
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
Make sure the die represents the correct size. | 1.
Make sure the inner cavity of the joint is completely clean. | 2.
Make sure the conductor ends are sound; if there is damage, cut off the damaged part. | 3.
Clean all parts of the conductor strands to be compressed, especially for greased conductors or old conductors; in the first case use a suitable solvent, and in the other case use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 4.
Put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of the joint, then put the conductors into the joint so that they reach the mark made previously (Figure x1a). | 5.
Compress the joint starting from the middle (Figure x1b) after leaving a distance of 2 cm from the centre on both sides, then continue compressing alternately from both sides until they overlap, and make sure of the appropriate pressure value shown on the pressure gauge. | 6.
Make sure the joint being compressed is completely horizontal so that it does not bend. | 7.
Clean the surface of the joint with a file so that there are no protrusions on the surface of the joint. | 8.
